Emma (support): Hey all – customer Jane is hitting structured-output/validation failures. They call /v1/generate with structured_mode=jsonschema and streaming=true. Sometimes we return 200 but the body is not valid JSON; their Pydantic client raises JSONDecodeError. They provided a short repro below.

Jane (customer): here's the request I used (redacted API key):
```json
{
  "model": "rw-large-1",
  "structured_mode": "jsonschema",
  "stream": true,
  "schema": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object" } },
  "prompt": "gen 3 items"
}
```

Jane (customer): actual response chunks they reassembled (the last chunk sometimes ends up as a trailing comma):
```
[
  {"id":1,"value":"a"},
  {"id":2,"value":"b"},
  {"id":3,"value":"c"},
]
```

Jane (customer): error from pydantic on their side: `JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 68 (char 67)` and `pydantic.error_wrappers.ValidationError: 1 validation error for List[Item]`

Sam (eng): can you paste the request-id / x-rw-request-id and the exact timestamp window? Also, is the SDK doing any client-side chunk concat or are you streaming into a file?

Emma (support): request-id: rq_0a9f3b2c, window: 2024-11-03T15:42:11Z -> 15:42:13Z. Customer is using requests.stream in Python and concatenating bytes as they arrive.

Micah (eng-ml): thanks, reproducing now. Quick notes: I can reproduce when stream=true and structured_mode=jsonschema. Looks like the streamer emits delimiting commas between items but in the last write path we sometimes still append a delimiter if the schema adapter flushes a short buffer after the final item — results in an extra `,` before the closing `]`. Minimal repro I ran:
```python
# pseudocode to repro client concat behavior
chunks = [b'[', b'{"id":1}', b',', b'{"id":2}', b',', b'{"id":3}', b',', b']']
# if network reorder or adapter flushes differently you can end up with trailing comma before final bracket.
```
Micah (eng-ml): root cause seems to be stream chunk boundary handling inside the schema adapter that inserts delimiters unconditionally when finishing a partial item. I have a local fix: only emit a delimiter when you know another item will follow (i.e., don't write a comma into the output buffer until the next item starts or on a confirmed next write).

Rebecca (devex): short-term workaround for affected customers: set `stream=false` (buffered response) or post-process the assembled bytes to sanitize trailing commas before parsing (e.g., rstrip and replace `,]` -> `]`). Example: `body = body.rstrip(); body = re.sub(r",\s*]$", "]", body)`

Emma (support): applied the workaround instructions to Jane and asked them to try stream=false. They confirmed buffered mode works and pydantic now validates.

oncall-bot: Created incident INC-2041 and linked the request-id rq_0a9f3b2c; priority P2. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2041

Micah (eng-ml): filed PR with fix to the schema adapter stream delimiter logic, branch: fix/stream-delimiter-avoid-trailing, draft commit abcdef1. My local tests and a small integration test that simulates chunk reorders pass.

Sam (eng): can you add a unit test that simulates client concat patterns (trailing delimiter + final bracket) and assert we never produce `,]`? Also add a quick e2e QA with rw-large-1 streaming to staging.

Micah (eng-ml): yes, adding both. I'll ping eng-releases when PR is ready for review.

Emma (support): I'll update Jane: workaround applied, fix on the way, ETA for rollout after reviews + staging QA ~ 48 hours. Will follow up with a postmortem in the ticket.

Rebecca (devex): note for docs: add a bullet under streaming/structured-output best practices about client concatenation and the temporary workaround.

Emma (support): thanks everyone :thumbsup: Jane will confirm after we deploy.

Jane (customer): thanks all — appreciate the quick triage.
